title: CPS school board president candidates Jessica Biggs, Victor Henderson, Hilario Dominguez await 2026 election results
text:
2026 election results: Jessica Biggs declares victory in CPS board president election against Victor Henderson, Hilario Dominguez - ABC7 Chicago

 Jessica Biggs declares victory in 1st-ever election for Chicago Board of Education president 
 Chicago voters are electing a school board president for the first time in a race that has been expensive, at times bitter, and historic. WLS By Sarah Schulte , Naomi Ruchim Wednesday, November 4, 2026 3:31AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- Jessica Biggs has declared victory in the first-ever election for Chicago Board of Education president.
 The following is from a previous report. 
 Chicago voters are electing a school board president for the first time in a race that has been expensive, at times bitter, and historic.
 The three candidates seeking the position - Jessica Biggs, Hilario Dominguez, and Victor Henderson - are backed by different political and labor coalitions, but all have said they are willing to work together if elected.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Biggs, a current school board member, a former special education teacher, and a former principal, has promoted what she describes as a broad coalition of supporters. Her endorsements include Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle and several unions.
 "I have over 400 donors and the support of SEIU, Chicago Federation of Labor, I've also drawn support from the business community, more than 20 alderpeople from across the city," Biggs said.
 That business support includes a $1 million donation from billionaire and Democratic donor Michael Sacks. Sacks is seeking to prevent the Chicago Teachers Union from controlling the school board.

 "This isn't about us or any one organization. This is about the city of Chicago being able to decide their leadership at their schools," Dominguez said.
 READ MORE | 2026 midterm elections: Voter information in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin 
 Dominguez, a former Chicago Teachers Union employee and a CPS graduate, has received most of his campaign funding from the union and its political action committee. While the Chicago Teachers Union and SEIU worked together to help elect Mayor Brandon Johnson, the unions later split during CTU contract negotiations.
 Henderson, a Chicago attorney who describes himself as an independent candidate, said the influence of competing organizations reflects broader problems within Chicago Public Schools.
 "It is emblematic of what's wrong with CPS is that you have these entities that have their own interests, you know, in this particular case, you're fighting over workers, which means money and power. That doesn't have anything to do with educating children," Henderson said.
 Henderson, the former president of the Chicago Bar Association, has largely self-funded his campaign.
 "I didn't want to be on anybody's payroll. I didn't want to be carrying anybody's water," he said.
 Despite their differing sources of support, Biggs and Dominguez said they would work with organizations that backed rival candidates.
 "My values are keeping us, children and our families at the center I'm going to work with anyone that is able to agree with that," Dominguez said.
 "It is it's tremendously important that we can come together and figure this out together. So, I fully intend to work with CTU," Biggs said.
 Nearly $9 million has been spent on the race, even though the position is voluntary. Biggs and Dominguez said they believe the school board president should be a paid position to attract a wider range of candidates.
